title: Negotiating an offer
settingKo: 입사 제안을 받은 뒤 조건을 협상합니다.

lines.text: We're delighted to offer you the role. Has the package we sent over met your expectations?
lines.ko: 이 자리를 제안하게 되어 기쁩니다. 보내 드린 조건이 기대에 맞으셨나요?

lines.text: I'm thrilled about the role itself, but the base salary is somewhat below what I had in mind.
lines.ko: 직무 자체는 정말 기쁘지만, 기본급이 생각했던 것보다 다소 낮습니다.

lines.text: I see. Is there a particular figure you were hoping for, and what's that based on?
lines.ko: 그렇군요. 원하시는 금액이 있나요? 근거는 무엇인가요?

lines.text: Given the market rate and the scope of the team I'd be managing, I was aiming for around ten percent more.
lines.ko: 시장 수준과 제가 맡을 팀 규모를 고려해 10% 정도 더 생각하고 있었습니다.

lines.text: There's limited room on base pay, but we may have some flexibility on the signing bonus.
lines.ko: 기본급은 여지가 적지만, 입사 보너스는 조정할 수 있을 것 같습니다.

lines.text: That could work, provided we revisit the salary at my first performance review.
lines.ko: 첫 성과 평가 때 연봉을 다시 논의한다면 괜찮을 것 같습니다.

gist.questionKo: 회사가 조정할 수 있다고 한 항목은?

phrases.en: It's somewhat below what I had in mind.
That could work, provided we revisit it later.
phrases.ko: 나중에 다시 논의한다면 괜찮을 것 같아요.

response.situationKo: 상대가 예산이 없어 인상은 불가능하다고 합니다. 관계를 해치지 않고 다른 조건을 끌어내 보세요.
response.prompt: I'm afraid the budget simply doesn't allow for a higher salary this year.

answers.text: I appreciate the constraints. Would there be any flexibility on remote days or additional leave instead?
answers.noteKo: 제약을 인정한 뒤 다른 조건으로 넘어가요.

answers.text: Understood. Could we agree to revisit it in six months, tied to clear performance targets?
That's a shame, but I'm open to creative solutions. What else might be on the table?
answers.noteKo: on the table은 논의 가능하다는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: Fair enough. Is it the base that's fixed, or the overall package?

title: The remote work debate
settingKo: 동료와 사무실 복귀 정책을 놓고 의견을 나눕니다.

lines.text: I know it's unpopular, but I think the return to the office is long overdue.
lines.ko: 인기 없는 의견인 건 알지만, 사무실 복귀는 진작 했어야 한다고 봐요.

lines.text: Really? The data I've seen suggests productivity hasn't suffered in the slightest.
lines.ko: 정말요? 제가 본 자료로는 생산성이 전혀 떨어지지 않았던데요.

lines.text: Output perhaps, but junior staff are missing out on the informal mentoring you only get in person.
lines.ko: 산출량은 그럴지 몰라도, 신입들은 직접 만나야만 얻는 비공식 멘토링을 놓치고 있어요.

lines.text: That's a fair point, though forcing everyone back seems like a blunt solution to a narrow problem.
lines.ko: 일리는 있지만, 전원 복귀는 좁은 문제에 대한 투박한 해결책 같아요.

lines.text: So what would you propose instead, a couple of anchor days each week?
lines.ko: 그럼 대안이 뭔가요, 일주일에 며칠 정해진 출근일을 두는 건가요?

lines.text: Exactly, as long as those days are used for collaboration rather than sitting on video calls.
lines.ko: 바로 그거예요. 그날은 화상 회의 대신 협업에 쓴다는 조건으로요.

phrases.en: That's a fair point, though...
It's long overdue.

response.situationKo: 동료가 강한 의견을 말합니다. 일부 인정하되 반론을 제시해 보세요.
response.prompt: Honestly, I think social media has done far more harm than good.

answers.text: That's a fair point, though I'd argue it's also given a voice to people who never had one.
answers.noteKo: 인정 후 반론을 펴는 대표적인 틀이에요.

answers.text: I see where you're coming from, but doesn't it depend on how people use it?
I'm not entirely convinced. The harm is real, but so are the benefits for small businesses.
You might be right, but I reckon that's a bit of a sweeping statement.
answers.noteKo: I reckon은 영국과 호주에서 I think처럼 써요.

title: Giving hard feedback
settingKo: 일을 잘하지만 회의에서 남의 말을 자주 끊는 팀원과 면담합니다.

lines.text: Thanks for making time. First, the analysis you delivered last week was outstanding.
lines.ko: 시간 내 줘서 고마워요. 우선 지난주 분석 결과는 정말 훌륭했어요.

lines.text: There is something I'd like to raise, though. In meetings, you tend to jump in before others have finished.
lines.ko: 그런데 말하고 싶은 게 있어요. 회의에서 다른 사람 말이 끝나기 전에 끼어드는 경향이 있어요.

lines.text: Oh, I hadn't realized it was coming across that way. I'm usually just excited about the idea.
lines.ko: 아, 그렇게 보이는 줄 몰랐어요. 보통 아이디어에 신이 나서 그래요.

lines.text: I believe that, and your energy is an asset. The trouble is quieter colleagues have started holding back.
lines.ko: 그렇겠죠, 그 열정은 장점이에요. 문제는 조용한 동료들이 말을 아끼기 시작했다는 거예요.

lines.text: That's hard to hear, but I appreciate you telling me. I'll make a point of letting people finish.
lines.ko: 듣기 힘들지만 말해 줘서 고마워요. 사람들 말을 끝까지 듣도록 신경 쓸게요.

phrases.en: There is something I'd like to raise.
I hadn't realized it was coming across that way.

response.situationKo: 동료가 마감을 또 놓치고 사과합니다. 비난하지 않으면서 문제를 분명히 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: I'm really sorry I missed the deadline again. Things have been hectic.

answers.text: I appreciate the apology, but this is the second time, and it's affecting the whole team. What's getting in the way?
answers.noteKo: 사실과 영향을 말한 뒤 원인을 물어요.

answers.text: I understand things are hectic. Going forward, could you flag it early if a date is at risk?
Thanks for owning it. I do need to be able to rely on these dates, so how can I help you hit the next one?
answers.noteKo: 책임을 인정해 준 뒤 기대치를 분명히 해요.

answers.text: No worries, but let's not make a habit of it, yeah?

title: Changing direction
settingKo: 경영진 회의에서 주력 제품 방향을 바꾸자고 제안합니다.

lines.text: Our consumer app has plateaued, but enterprise clients keep asking whether they can use it with their teams.
lines.ko: 소비자 앱은 정체됐는데 기업 고객들은 팀 단위로 쓸 수 있냐고 계속 묻습니다.

lines.text: Are you suggesting we abandon the consumer side entirely? That's where our brand comes from.
lines.ko: 소비자 쪽을 완전히 버리자는 건가요? 우리 브랜드가 거기서 나왔는데요.

lines.text: Not abandon, but stop investing in growth there and redirect most of the engineering effort to a team version.
lines.ko: 버리자는 게 아니라 거기 성장 투자는 멈추고 개발 인력 대부분을 팀 버전으로 돌리자는 거예요.

lines.text: I'd want to see a revenue forecast before I'd be comfortable taking that to the board.
lines.ko: 이사회에 올리기 전에 매출 전망부터 보고 싶네요.

phrases.en: Our consumer app has plateaued.
I'd want to see a forecast before taking it to the board.
phrases.ko: 이사회에 올리기 전에 전망부터 보고 싶네요.

response.situationKo: 임원이 위험이 크다고 반대합니다. 근거를 들어 설득해 보세요.
response.prompt: This feels risky. What if enterprise sales take longer than you think?

answers.text: That's a fair point, which is why I'm proposing a phased rollout with clear checkpoints.
Even if sales take longer, we'd still be reducing costs on a product that isn't growing.
answers.noteKo: Even if로 최악의 경우도 대비했다고 보여 줘요.

answers.text: The data from our pilot clients suggests the sales cycle is shorter than we assumed.
I hear you. Let's agree on what numbers would make us stop, so the risk is capped.

title: A difficult conversation
settingKo: 최근 성과가 떨어진 팀원과 조심스럽게 면담합니다.

lines.text: I've noticed a few missed deadlines lately, which isn't like you. Is something going on that I should know about?
lines.ko: 최근 마감을 몇 번 놓쳤는데 당신답지 않아요. 내가 알아야 할 일이 있나요?

lines.text: My father has been in and out of hospital, and I haven't been sleeping much.
lines.ko: 아버지가 입퇴원을 반복하셔서 잠을 거의 못 자고 있어요.

lines.text: I'm really sorry. Let's look at reducing your workload for a few weeks and maybe adjusting your hours.
lines.ko: 정말 안타까워요. 몇 주간 업무량을 줄이고 근무 시간을 조정하는 걸 검토해 봐요.

lines.text: That would make a huge difference. I didn't want to bring it up because I thought it might look like an excuse.
lines.ko: 그럼 정말 큰 도움이 될 거예요. 핑계처럼 보일까 봐 말을 못 꺼냈어요.

phrases.en: That isn't like you.
I didn't want it to look like an excuse.

response.situationKo: 팀원의 실수가 반복됩니다. 비난하지 않고 문제를 짚어 보세요.
response.prompt: Is there something you wanted to talk to me about?

answers.text: I've noticed a pattern of small errors in the reports. Can you help me understand what's happening?
answers.noteKo: help me understand는 비난 없이 이유를 묻는 표현이에요.

answers.text: I wanted to check in, because the last few deliverables needed a lot of rework.
Let's figure out together what support you need to get back on track.
answers.noteKo: get back on track은 정상 궤도로 돌아오다예요.

answers.text: Hey, no judgment here, but something seems off lately. What can we do?

title: Terms of the partnership
settingKo: 다른 회사와 제휴 계약의 수익 배분을 협상합니다.

lines.text: We're proposing a sixty-forty revenue split, given that our platform brings in the majority of the users.
lines.ko: 저희 플랫폼이 사용자 대부분을 데려오니 6대 4 수익 배분을 제안합니다.

lines.text: I see the logic, but our content is what keeps those users engaged once they arrive.
lines.ko: 논리는 이해하지만 들어온 사용자를 붙잡는 건 저희 콘텐츠예요.

lines.text: Would you be open to fifty-fifty for the first year, with a review based on actual retention data?
lines.ko: 첫해는 5대 5로 하고 실제 유지율 데이터로 재검토하는 건 어떠세요?

lines.text: That's reasonable, provided the review criteria are agreed in writing upfront.
lines.ko: 검토 기준을 미리 서면으로 합의한다면 합리적이에요.

phrases.en: I see the logic, but...
Provided the criteria are agreed in writing.

response.situationKo: 상대가 불리한 조건을 고집합니다. 관계를 해치지 않으며 버텨 보세요.
response.prompt: Honestly, sixty-forty is our final offer.

answers.text: I appreciate your position. However, at sixty-forty the deal doesn't work for us financially.
answers.noteKo: doesn't work for us는 '우리에겐 맞지 않는다'예요.

answers.text: Before we walk away, can we get creative? Maybe a bonus tied to retention?
answers.noteKo: get creative는 다른 방식을 찾아보자는 말이에요.

answers.text: We value this partnership long-term, so let's find a middle ground we can both defend internally.
answers.noteKo: defend internally는 내부를 설득할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: Final, huh? Then I think we're stuck, unless there's flexibility somewhere else.

title: Handling a product recall
settingKo: 제품 결함이 SNS에 퍼져 홍보팀과 대응 방안을 논의합니다.

lines.text: The video of the charger overheating has two million views. We need to respond within the hour.
lines.ko: 충전기 과열 영상이 조회수 200만이에요. 한 시간 안에 대응해야 해요.

lines.text: Legal wants us to wait until testing is complete, but silence will look like we're hiding something.
lines.ko: 법무팀은 검사가 끝날 때까지 기다리자는데 침묵하면 뭔가 숨기는 것처럼 보일 거예요.

lines.text: Then let's acknowledge it, pause sales, and promise a full update within forty-eight hours.
lines.ko: 그럼 인정하고 판매를 중단하고 48시간 내 전체 업데이트를 약속하죠.

lines.text: Agreed. And the CEO should record the message herself, not hide behind a press release.
lines.ko: 동의해요. 보도자료 뒤에 숨지 말고 CEO가 직접 메시지를 녹화해야 해요.

phrases.en: Silence will look like we're hiding something.
phrases.ko: 침묵하면 뭔가 숨기는 것처럼 보일 거예요.

phrases.en: Don't hide behind a press release.

response.situationKo: 기자가 회사의 실수에 대해 묻습니다. 책임감 있게 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why should customers trust your company after this?

answers.text: We take full responsibility, and we'll publish every test result as soon as we have it.
answers.noteKo: take full responsibility는 전적인 책임을 지다예요.

answers.text: Trust has to be earned back, and the way we do that is by being transparent at every step.
Here's what we're doing right now: pausing sales, contacting every buyer, and offering refunds.
Honestly, they shouldn't just take our word for it. Judge us on what we do next.

title: Is the algorithm fair?
settingKo: AI 채용 도구 도입을 두고 인사팀과 윤리 문제를 토론합니다.

lines.text: The screening tool cut our hiring time in half, so I'm not sure what the objection is.
lines.ko: 선별 도구로 채용 기간이 반으로 줄었는데 반대 이유를 모르겠어요.

lines.text: It was trained on our past hires, so it may simply be repeating the biases we already had.
lines.ko: 과거 합격자로 학습했으니 우리가 이미 가진 편향을 그대로 반복하고 있을 수 있어요.

lines.text: That's a valid concern. How would we even know if that's happening?
lines.ko: 타당한 우려네요. 그런 일이 일어나는지 어떻게 알 수 있죠?

lines.text: We'd need an independent audit comparing outcomes across gender, age, and background.
lines.ko: 성별, 나이, 배경별 결과를 비교하는 독립 감사가 필요해요.

phrases.en: It may simply be repeating our biases.
phrases.ko: 편향을 그대로 반복하고 있을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: That's a valid concern.

response.situationKo: 기술 도입에 대해 균형 잡힌 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Should companies use AI to screen job applications?

answers.text: On the one hand it saves time, but on the other, it can hide unfair decisions.
answers.noteKo: On the one hand ~ on the other로 양면을 말해요.

answers.text: I'd argue it's acceptable as long as a human makes the final decision.
answers.noteKo: I'd argue는 논리적 주장을 펼칠 때 써요.

answers.text: Only if there's real oversight and candidates can ask why they were rejected.
Honestly, I'm skeptical. Hiring is too human to hand over to a model.

title: Questions from investors
settingKo: 스타트업 대표가 투자 설명회에서 날카로운 질문을 받습니다.

lines.text: Your growth is impressive, but your customer acquisition cost has doubled in six months. Why?
lines.ko: 성장은 인상적이지만 고객 획득 비용이 6개월 만에 두 배가 됐네요. 왜죠?

lines.text: We deliberately expanded into two new markets, and early costs are always higher before word of mouth kicks in.
lines.ko: 의도적으로 신규 시장 두 곳에 진출했고, 입소문이 나기 전 초기 비용은 늘 더 높아요.

lines.text: And if word of mouth doesn't kick in?
lines.ko: 입소문이 안 나면요?

lines.text: Then we pull back to our core market, where we're already profitable on every customer.
lines.ko: 그러면 고객마다 이미 수익이 나는 핵심 시장으로 후퇴합니다.

phrases.en: Before word of mouth kicks in.
We pull back to our core market.

response.situationKo: 투자자가 경쟁사가 더 크다고 지적합니다. 차별점을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Your competitor has ten times your funding. Why will you win?

answers.text: Because we're focused on one customer segment they treat as an afterthought.
Unlike them, our customers stay. Our retention is nearly twice theirs.
Funding buys reach, not loyalty. Our advantage is a product people genuinely recommend.
Big doesn't mean fast. We ship in weeks what they ship in quarters.

title: Advice from a mentor
settingKo: 경력 많은 멘토에게 커리어 고민을 털어놓습니다.

lines.text: I've been offered a management role, but I'm worried I'll miss the hands-on work I actually enjoy.
lines.ko: 관리자 자리를 제안받았는데 정말 좋아하는 실무를 그리워하게 될까 봐 걱정돼요.

lines.text: That's a common fear, and it's worth taking seriously. Not everyone is happier as a manager.
lines.ko: 흔한 두려움이고 진지하게 생각할 만해요. 모두가 관리자로서 더 행복한 건 아니에요.

lines.text: Ask whether there's a senior expert track. Many companies pay specialists just as well now.
lines.ko: 시니어 전문가 트랙이 있는지 물어봐요. 요즘은 전문가에게도 똑같이 대우하는 회사가 많아요.

lines.text: I hadn't even considered that. I assumed management was the only way up.
lines.ko: 그건 생각도 못 했어요. 관리직만 올라가는 길인 줄 알았어요.

phrases.en: It's worth taking seriously.
I assumed it was the only way up.
phrases.ko: 그게 유일한 승진 길인 줄 알았어요.

response.situationKo: 후배가 커리어 조언을 구합니다. 경험을 바탕으로 조언해 보세요.
response.prompt: If you could give your younger self one piece of career advice, what would it be?

answers.text: I'd tell myself to worry less about titles and more about who I was learning from.
answers.noteKo: worry less about A and more about B 구조예요.

answers.text: Take more risks early, when the cost of failing is low.
answers.noteKo: when the cost is low로 이유를 붙여요.

answers.text: Build relationships before you need them. The people matter more than the job.
Honestly? Ask for the raise. Nobody's going to offer it unless you do.

title: Resigning gracefully
settingKo: 오래 함께한 상사에게 퇴사를 알립니다.

lines.text: This isn't an easy conversation, but I've accepted an offer elsewhere, and my last day would be the twentieth.
lines.ko: 쉽지 않은 얘기인데요, 다른 곳 제안을 수락해서 마지막 날이 20일이 될 것 같아요.

lines.text: I'm sorry to lose you, but I'm not entirely surprised. Can I ask what tipped the balance?
lines.ko: 잃게 돼서 아쉽지만 완전히 놀랍지는 않네요. 뭐가 결정적이었는지 물어봐도 될까요?

lines.text: Mainly the chance to lead a team, which I know wasn't going to happen here for a while.
lines.ko: 주로 팀을 이끌 기회요. 여기서는 한동안 어렵다는 걸 알고 있었거든요.

lines.text: I'll make sure the handover is thorough, and I'm happy to help train my replacement.
lines.ko: 인수인계는 꼼꼼히 하고 후임자 교육도 기꺼이 돕겠습니다.

phrases.en: What tipped the balance?
I'll make sure the handover is thorough.

response.situationKo: 상사가 연봉을 올려 줄 테니 남으라고 합니다. 정중히 거절해 보세요.
response.prompt: What if we matched their offer? Would you stay?

answers.text: I'm grateful, truly, but it's not about the money. It's about the role.
answers.noteKo: it's not about A, it's about B 구조예요.

answers.text: I really appreciate that, but I've made my decision, and I'd like to leave on good terms.
answers.noteKo: leave on good terms는 좋게 떠나다예요.

answers.text: That's generous, but I think staying for the money would be unfair to both of us.
Ah, that means a lot. But I need to try this, or I'll always wonder.

title: Exit interview
settingKo: 인사팀과 퇴사 면담에서 솔직한 피드백을 줍니다.

lines.text: Is there anything we could have done differently that might have made you stay?
lines.ko: 당신이 남을 수 있도록 우리가 다르게 할 수 있었던 게 있을까요?

lines.text: Clearer promotion criteria, honestly. People never knew what they had to achieve to move up.
lines.ko: 솔직히 승진 기준이 더 명확했으면 해요. 다들 무엇을 이뤄야 올라가는지 몰랐어요.

lines.text: That's come up in several interviews this year. Was there anything you'd want us to keep?
lines.ko: 올해 여러 면담에서 나온 얘기예요. 유지했으면 하는 건 있나요?

lines.text: The flexibility and the people. My team was the best I've ever worked with.
lines.ko: 유연성과 사람들이요. 우리 팀은 제가 일해 본 중 최고였어요.

phrases.en: That's come up several times.
The best I've ever worked with.

response.situationKo: 회사에 건설적인 비판을 해 보세요.
response.prompt: Be candid. What's one thing this company gets wrong?

answers.text: Candidly, decisions take too long because too many people need to sign off.
One thing is communication. We often hear about changes from clients before our own managers.
I think we reward people for being busy rather than for being effective.
Too many meetings that could've been emails, honestly.

title: Getting a second opinion
settingKo: 수술을 권유받은 후 다른 전문의에게 의견을 묻습니다.

lines.text: My first doctor recommended surgery on my knee, but I wanted to understand all my options first.
lines.ko: 첫 의사는 무릎 수술을 권했는데 먼저 모든 선택지를 알고 싶었어요.

lines.text: That's sensible. Looking at your scans, surgery is one option, but it isn't urgent.
lines.ko: 현명하네요. 영상을 보면 수술도 한 방법이지만 급하지는 않아요.

lines.text: Many patients with this kind of tear improve significantly with three months of physical therapy.
lines.ko: 이런 파열은 3개월 물리치료로 크게 좋아지는 환자가 많아요.

lines.text: So it would be reasonable to try therapy first and keep surgery as a backup?
lines.ko: 그럼 치료를 먼저 해 보고 수술은 대안으로 남겨 두는 게 합리적일까요?

phrases.en: I wanted to understand all my options.
Keep surgery as a backup.

response.situationKo: 의사에게 치료 선택지에 대해 깊이 있게 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Do you have any questions before we decide on a treatment?

answers.text: What are the risks if I wait, compared with having the operation now?
How likely is it that physical therapy alone will be enough?
In your experience, what does recovery actually look like day to day?
If it were your knee, what would you do?

title: Caring for Dad
settingKo: 형제와 연로하신 아버지의 돌봄 문제를 의논합니다.

lines.text: Dad fell again last week. I don't think he can keep living on his own, even if he insists he's fine.
lines.ko: 아빠가 지난주에 또 넘어지셨어. 괜찮다고 우기셔도 혼자 사시긴 어려울 것 같아.

lines.text: I agree, but he'll be heartbroken if we suggest a care home. That house is his whole life.
lines.ko: 동의해. 그런데 요양원 얘기를 꺼내면 상심하실 거야. 그 집이 아빠 인생 전부잖아.

lines.text: What about a caregiver who comes in every morning? We could split the cost three ways.
lines.ko: 매일 아침 오는 간병인은 어때? 비용은 셋이 나누면 되고.

lines.text: That feels like a good compromise, as long as we involve him in the decision rather than tell him.
lines.ko: 좋은 절충안 같아. 통보하지 말고 결정에 아빠를 참여시킨다면.

phrases.en: Even if he insists he's fine.
Involve him in the decision rather than tell him.

response.situationKo: 가족 중 한 명이 부담을 다 지고 있어요. 공평하게 나누자고 제안해 보세요.
response.prompt: I've been doing most of the hospital visits on my own, you know.

answers.text: You're right, and I'm sorry. Let's set up a rotation so it's not all on you.
That's not fair to you. I can take every Saturday from now on.
I hadn't realized how much you were carrying. Thank you, and let's share it properly.
Ugh, I've been useless. Put me on the schedule, seriously.

title: Getting my deposit back
settingKo: 이사 후 보증금을 부당하게 깎은 집주인과 통화합니다.

lines.text: You've deducted eight hundred for repainting, but the walls were already marked when I moved in.
lines.ko: 재도색 비용으로 800을 공제하셨는데 입주할 때 이미 벽에 자국이 있었어요.

lines.text: I don't remember that. The walls looked fine to me.
lines.ko: 기억이 안 나네요. 저한텐 벽이 괜찮아 보였어요.

lines.text: I have dated photos from move-in day, and normal wear and tear can't legally be charged to the tenant.
lines.ko: 입주일 날짜가 찍힌 사진이 있고, 통상적인 마모는 법적으로 세입자에게 청구할 수 없어요.

lines.text: Send me the photos, and if they show that, I'll return the full amount.
lines.ko: 사진 보내 주세요. 그렇다면 전액 돌려드릴게요.

phrases.en: The walls were already marked when I moved in.
phrases.ko: 입주할 때 이미 벽에 자국이 있었어요.

phrases.en: Normal wear and tear.

response.situationKo: 상대가 근거 없이 요금을 청구합니다. 단호하게 증거를 요구해 보세요.
response.prompt: There's an additional cleaning charge of two hundred dollars.

answers.text: On what basis? I'd like to see an itemized invoice and photos of the problem.
I left the apartment spotless. Could you provide evidence for that charge?
I'm going to dispute that, since it wasn't mentioned at the final inspection.
Two hundred? For what, exactly? I need details before I pay anything.

title: Reading the fine print
settingKo: 프리랜서 계약서의 불리한 조항을 의뢰인과 논의합니다.

lines.text: Clause seven says you own everything I create during the contract, including personal projects.
lines.ko: 7조에 계약 기간 중 제가 만든 모든 것, 개인 프로젝트까지 귀사 소유라고 되어 있어요.

lines.text: That's our standard wording. Legal tends to be cautious.
lines.ko: 저희 표준 문구예요. 법무팀이 신중한 편이라서요.

lines.text: I understand, but I'd need it limited to work that's produced for you and paid for by you.
lines.ko: 이해하지만 귀사를 위해 만들고 귀사가 비용을 낸 작업으로 한정해야 해요.

lines.text: That seems fair. I'll ask them to narrow the scope and send you a revised draft.
lines.ko: 공정해 보이네요. 범위를 좁혀 달라고 해서 수정안을 보내 드릴게요.

phrases.en: Legal tends to be cautious.
I'll ask them to narrow the scope.

response.situationKo: 계약서에 지급 기한이 너무 길어요. 수정을 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: Does the rest of the contract look OK to you?

answers.text: Mostly, yes. One thing: ninety-day payment terms are too long for a freelancer. Could we do thirty?
Would it be possible to get half upfront and half on delivery?
It's fine except for payment. Ninety days would really hurt my cash flow.
Almost! Can we fix the payment timeline, though? Thirty days is standard for me.

title: Challenging a claim
settingKo: 대학원 세미나에서 발표자의 주장에 이의를 제기합니다.

lines.text: Your data shows a correlation between screen time and anxiety, but couldn't the causation run the other way?
lines.ko: 데이터는 화면 시간과 불안의 상관관계를 보여 주는데, 인과 관계가 반대일 수도 있지 않나요?

lines.text: Good question. You mean anxious people might simply spend more time on screens?
lines.ko: 좋은 질문이에요. 불안한 사람이 화면을 더 오래 볼 수도 있다는 뜻이죠?

lines.text: Exactly. Without a longitudinal study, it's hard to rule that out.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 종단 연구 없이는 그 가능성을 배제하기 어려워요.

lines.text: That's a fair limitation, and it's actually what our follow-up study is designed to address.
lines.ko: 타당한 한계예요. 사실 후속 연구가 그걸 다루도록 설계됐어요.

phrases.en: Couldn't the causation run the other way?
phrases.ko: 인과 관계가 반대일 수도 있지 않나요?

phrases.en: It's hard to rule that out.

response.situationKo: 발표 후 누군가 날카롭게 반박합니다. 인정할 건 인정하며 방어해 보세요.
response.prompt: Isn't your sample far too small to draw that conclusion?

answers.text: That's a fair point, which is why I described the results as preliminary.
I'd agree it's a limitation. However, the effect was consistent across every subgroup.
It's small, yes, but it's enough to suggest the question deserves a larger study.
Totally fair. I'm not claiming the final answer, just a strong hint.

title: All the world's a stage
settingKo: 친구와 셰익스피어의 유명한 구절에 대해 이야기합니다.

lines.text: There's a line from As You Like It I keep thinking about: All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players.
lines.ko: '뜻대로 하세요'의 구절이 계속 생각나: 온 세상은 무대이고 모든 남녀는 배우일 뿐.

lines.text: It's over four hundred years old, but it describes social media perfectly. Everyone is performing.
lines.ko: 400년도 넘은 말인데 SNS를 완벽하게 묘사하네. 다들 연기하잖아.

lines.text: Shakespeare meant the stages of life, though, from childhood to old age.
lines.ko: 셰익스피어는 어린 시절부터 노년까지 인생의 단계를 말한 거긴 해.

lines.text: True, but great lines survive precisely because every generation finds a new meaning in them.
lines.ko: 맞아, 그래도 명구절은 세대마다 새 의미를 찾기 때문에 살아남는 거야.

phrases.en: All the world's a stage.
Every generation finds a new meaning in them.

response.situationKo: 좋아하는 명언이나 구절을 소개하고 이유를 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you have a favorite quote? Why does it stick with you?

answers.text: My favorite is 'To thine own self be true' from Hamlet. It reminds me not to pretend.
I love 'The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.' It's from Roosevelt, and it calms me down.
'Well done is better than well said.' Benjamin Franklin. It's basically my work motto.
It's a proverb: 'A smooth sea never made a skilled sailor.' Hard times teach us the most.
answers.noteKo: 잔잔한 바다는 숙련된 선원을 만들지 못한다는 속담이에요.

title: Of the people, by the people
settingKo: 토론 수업에서 링컨의 게티즈버그 연설을 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Lincoln's Gettysburg Address is only about two hundred and seventy words, yet it's one of the most quoted speeches in history.
lines.ko: 링컨의 게티즈버그 연설은 270단어 정도밖에 안 되는데 역사상 가장 많이 인용되는 연설 중 하나예요.

lines.text: The ending is what everyone remembers: government of the people, by the people, for the people.
lines.ko: 다들 기억하는 건 마지막이죠: 국민의, 국민에 의한, 국민을 위한 정부.

lines.text: What strikes me is how much he says by leaving things out. There's no list of battles or enemies.
lines.ko: 제가 놀라운 건 빼서 더 많은 걸 말한다는 점이에요. 전투나 적의 목록이 없어요.

lines.text: That's a lesson for any presentation. Brevity forces you to decide what actually matters.
lines.ko: 모든 발표에 주는 교훈이죠. 간결함은 정말 중요한 걸 정하게 만들어요.

phrases.en: Government of the people, by the people, for the people.
phrases.ko: 국민의, 국민에 의한, 국민을 위한 정부. (링컨)

phrases.en: Brevity forces you to decide what matters.

response.situationKo: 연설이나 발표를 잘하는 비결에 대한 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What do you think makes a speech memorable?

answers.text: I think it's one clear idea that the audience can repeat afterwards.
answers.noteKo: repeat afterwards는 나중에 따라 말할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: People remember stories, not statistics. A single personal example goes a long way.
answers.noteKo: goes a long way는 큰 효과가 있다는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: Keep it short and end with a line people want to quote.
Honestly, confidence. A simple speech delivered with conviction beats a clever one read off slides.

title: Old sayings, new situations
settingKo: 동료와 일하면서 영어 속담을 자연스럽게 섞어 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Should we launch next week with the bugs we know about, or wait another month?
lines.ko: 알고 있는 버그를 안고 다음 주에 출시할까, 한 달 더 기다릴까?

lines.text: Well, perfect is the enemy of good. If the bugs are minor, I'd launch and fix as we go.
lines.ko: 글쎄, 완벽은 좋음의 적이라잖아. 사소한 버그면 출시하고 진행하면서 고칠래.

lines.text: Fair, but once bitten, twice shy. Last time a small bug cost us our biggest client.
lines.ko: 맞아, 그래도 한 번 데면 조심하게 되잖아. 지난번엔 작은 버그 때문에 제일 큰 고객을 잃었어.

lines.text: Then let's not put all our eggs in one basket. Launch to ten percent of users first.
lines.ko: 그럼 한 바구니에 모든 달걀을 담지 말자. 먼저 사용자 10퍼센트에게만 출시하자.

phrases.en: Perfect is the enemy of good.
Don't put all your eggs in one basket.
phrases.ko: 한 바구니에 모든 달걀을 담지 마라.

response.situationKo: 친구가 큰 결정을 망설입니다. 속담을 섞어 조언해 보세요.
response.prompt: I want to start my own business, but what if it fails?

answers.text: Nothing ventured, nothing gained. Start small so the risk is manageable.
answers.noteKo: 모험하지 않으면 얻는 것도 없다는 속담이에요.

answers.text: Fortune favors the bold, as they say. But have six months of savings first.
You'll never know if you don't try. Failing isn't the worst outcome; regret is.
Go for it! Worst case, you learn a ton and get a job again.

title: A four-day week?
settingKo: 주 4일 근무제 도입을 두고 동료와 찬반을 토론합니다.

lines.text: The trials in the UK showed productivity held steady while burnout dropped. Why not try it here?
lines.ko: 영국 실험에서는 생산성은 유지되고 번아웃은 줄었어요. 여기서도 해 보면 어때요?

lines.text: Those were mostly office jobs. Our support team has to answer customers five days a week regardless.
lines.ko: 대부분 사무직이었잖아요. 우리 고객지원팀은 어쨌든 주 5일 응대해야 해요.

lines.text: Staggered days off could solve that. Half the team takes Monday, half takes Friday.
lines.ko: 쉬는 날을 엇갈리게 하면 돼요. 절반은 월요일, 절반은 금요일 쉬고요.

lines.text: Maybe, but I'd want a six-month pilot with clear metrics before committing.
lines.ko: 그럴 수도요. 그래도 확정 전에 명확한 지표로 6개월 시범을 해 보고 싶어요.

phrases.en: Productivity held steady.
Before committing.

response.situationKo: 주 4일제에 대한 내 입장을 근거와 함께 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: So where do you stand on the four-day week?

answers.text: I'm in favor, because rested people make fewer mistakes and stay longer.
In principle I like it, but I worry the work would just get squeezed into four longer days.
I'm torn. The evidence looks good, but it might not suit every industry.
Honestly? Sign me up. Three-day weekends forever.

title: Guest on a podcast
settingKo: 팟캐스트에 게스트로 나가 자신의 일에 대해 이야기합니다.

lines.text: You left a stable job at a bank to start a bakery. What was going through your mind?
lines.ko: 은행의 안정적인 직장을 그만두고 빵집을 차리셨죠. 그때 무슨 생각이었나요?

lines.text: Mostly fear, to be honest. But I'd reached a point where staying felt riskier than leaving.
lines.ko: 솔직히 대부분 두려움이었어요. 하지만 남는 게 떠나는 것보다 더 위험하게 느껴지는 지점에 왔었어요.

lines.text: That's an interesting way to put it. What made staying feel risky?
lines.ko: 흥미로운 표현이네요. 남는 게 왜 위험하게 느껴졌어요?

lines.text: I realized I'd wake up at sixty having spent my whole life on something I didn't care about.
lines.ko: 예순에 눈을 떴을 때 관심도 없는 일에 평생을 쓴 걸 알게 될 것 같았어요.

options: 관심 없는 일에 평생을 쓸 것 같아서

phrases.en: What was going through your mind?
Staying felt riskier than leaving.
phrases.ko: 남는 게 떠나는 것보다 더 위험하게 느껴졌어요.

response.situationKo: 인터뷰어가 가장 힘들었던 순간을 묻습니다. 이야기처럼 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: What was the hardest moment in that whole journey?

answers.text: Probably the first winter, when sales dropped by half and I seriously considered giving up.
I remember sitting in the empty shop at midnight, wondering if I'd made a terrible mistake.
Looking back, the hardest part was asking for help. I thought I had to do everything alone.
Oh, easy. The day the oven broke during our biggest order. Total chaos.

title: Is that actually true?
settingKo: 뉴스룸에서 편집자와 기자가 기사의 사실 관계를 확인합니다.

lines.text: You say crime rose thirty percent, but the police data only covers the last eight months.
lines.ko: 범죄가 30퍼센트 늘었다고 했는데 경찰 데이터는 최근 8개월뿐이에요.

lines.text: That's true. I compared it with the same period last year, which was unusually quiet.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 이례적으로 조용했던 작년 같은 기간과 비교했어요.

lines.text: Then the headline is misleading. Readers will assume it's a long-term trend.
lines.ko: 그럼 제목이 오해를 불러요. 독자들은 장기 추세라고 생각할 거예요.

lines.text: Fair enough. I'll add the five-year average and soften the headline.
lines.ko: 맞는 말이에요. 5년 평균을 추가하고 제목 수위를 낮출게요.

options: 단기 데이터를 장기 추세처럼 보이게 했다

phrases.en: The headline is misleading.
I'll soften the headline.

response.situationKo: 친구가 출처가 의심스러운 기사를 공유합니다. 조심스럽게 짚어 보세요.
response.prompt: Did you see this? Coffee apparently doubles your lifespan!

answers.text: Hmm, where is it from? I'd want to see the actual study before believing it.
I'd be careful with that. It's probably a correlation, not proof that coffee causes it.
Sounds too good to be true, honestly. Who funded the research?
answers.noteKo: too good to be true는 '믿기엔 너무 좋은'이에요.

answers.text: Ha, I wish! Let me guess, the source is a coffee company?

title: Reviewing a restaurant
settingKo: 고급 레스토랑 코스 요리를 먹은 뒤 친구와 냉정하게 평가합니다.

lines.text: The presentation was stunning, but I'm not convinced the flavors lived up to the price.
lines.ko: 플레이팅은 훌륭했는데 맛이 가격만큼이었는지는 모르겠어.

lines.text: The scallop course was exceptional, though. Everything else felt a bit safe.
lines.ko: 그래도 관자 코스는 탁월했어. 나머지는 좀 무난했고.

lines.text: Exactly. For three hundred dollars, I expect to be surprised at least once more.
lines.ko: 그러니까. 300달러면 적어도 한 번은 더 놀라길 기대하지.

lines.text: I'd go back for a special occasion, but I wouldn't recommend it to someone on a budget.
lines.ko: 특별한 날이면 다시 가겠지만 예산이 빠듯한 사람에겐 추천 안 할래.

phrases.en: I'm not convinced it lived up to the price.
Everything else felt a bit safe.

response.situationKo: 최근 경험한 서비스나 장소를 섬세하게 평가해 보세요.
response.prompt: So, was it worth the hype?

answers.text: Partly. The view lived up to the hype, but the service was disappointingly slow.
I'd say it's slightly overrated, although I can see why people love it.
Honestly, yes. Every bit worth it. I'm already planning to go back.
answers.noteKo: Every bit worth it은 '충분히 가치 있어'예요.

answers.text: Worth it once, for the experience, but not something I'd do regularly.

title: What does it mean?
settingKo: 현대 미술관에서 친구와 추상화를 두고 해석을 나눕니다.

lines.text: I'll be honest, I don't get it. It's just a grey square with a single red line.
lines.ko: 솔직히 이해가 안 돼. 회색 사각형에 빨간 선 하나잖아.

lines.text: The label says she painted it the year after her brother died. Maybe the line is the grief cutting through everything.
lines.ko: 설명엔 오빠가 죽은 다음 해에 그렸대. 그 선이 모든 걸 가르는 슬픔일지도 몰라.

lines.text: Huh. Knowing that, it suddenly feels much heavier.
lines.ko: 흠. 그걸 알고 나니 갑자기 훨씬 무겁게 느껴지네.

lines.text: That's what I love about abstract art. It gives you space to bring your own story to it.
lines.ko: 그게 추상화의 좋은 점이야. 자기 이야기를 가져올 여지를 주거든.

phrases.en: Knowing that, it suddenly feels heavier.
phrases.ko: 그걸 알고 나니 갑자기 무겁게 느껴지네.

phrases.en: It gives you space to bring your own story.

response.situationKo: 친구가 이해하기 어려운 작품에 대한 생각을 묻습니다. 자신만의 해석을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What do you see in this painting?

answers.text: To me, it feels like a city at night, crowded but somehow lonely.
I get the sense the artist was angry. Look at how rough the brushstrokes are.
It reminds me of my grandmother's kitchen, oddly enough. Maybe it's the colors.
I'm not sure, but I can't stop looking at it, which probably means something.

title: Working with an architect
settingKo: 건축가와 오래된 집 리모델링 방향을 논의합니다.

lines.text: If we remove this wall, the kitchen and living room become one open space, but it's load-bearing.
lines.ko: 이 벽을 없애면 주방과 거실이 하나로 트이지만 내력벽이에요.

lines.text: So it's possible, but expensive? How much would the steel beam add to the budget?
lines.ko: 가능은 하지만 비싸다는 거죠? 철제 보가 예산에 얼마나 더해질까요?

lines.text: Roughly fifteen thousand, plus about three extra weeks for permits.
lines.ko: 대략 1만 5천에 허가로 3주 정도가 더 걸려요.

lines.text: Let's get a structural engineer's opinion before we commit to anything.
lines.ko: 뭔가 확정하기 전에 구조 기술자 의견부터 들어 보죠.

phrases.en: It's load-bearing.
Before we commit to anything.

response.situationKo: 시공업자가 예산을 초과하는 안을 제시합니다. 우선순위를 정해 조정해 보세요.
response.prompt: With everything you want, we're about thirty percent over budget.

answers.text: Let's prioritize. The kitchen is non-negotiable, but the bathroom could wait a year.
What if we did the work in two phases, so the cost is spread out?
Could we use less expensive materials in the rooms guests rarely see?
Ouch. OK, what are the three things you'd cut first if it were your house?

title: A bidding war
settingKo: 마음에 드는 집에 여러 명이 입찰해 중개인과 전략을 세웁니다.

lines.text: There are four other offers, and at least two are above the asking price.
lines.ko: 다른 제안이 네 건 있고 적어도 두 건은 호가보다 높아요.

lines.text: We can't go much higher. Is there anything besides price that might make our offer stand out?
lines.ko: 더 올리긴 어려워요. 가격 말고 우리 제안을 돋보이게 할 방법이 있을까요?

lines.text: Sellers often value certainty. A quick closing and fewer conditions can matter as much as money.
lines.ko: 매도인은 확실성을 중시해요. 빠른 잔금과 조건 축소가 돈만큼 중요할 수 있어요.

lines.text: Then let's offer to close in thirty days and waive the request for new appliances.
lines.ko: 그럼 30일 내 잔금을 제안하고 새 가전 요청은 빼죠.

phrases.en: Make our offer stand out.
Sellers often value certainty.

response.situationKo: 중개인이 예산을 넘겨서라도 입찰하라고 권합니다. 신중하게 대응해 보세요.
response.prompt: If you really want it, I'd go another twenty thousand higher.

answers.text: We set a limit for a reason. I'd rather lose this house than be stretched for ten years.
I appreciate the advice, but that's beyond our limit. We'll walk away if necessary.
It's tempting, but no house is worth that kind of stress.
Ha, nice try. Our number is our number.
answers.noteKo: Our number is our number는 '우리 한도는 그대로'예요.

title: Declining diplomatically
settingKo: 업계 행사 연사 초청을 정중하게 거절합니다.

lines.text: We'd be honored if you could deliver the keynote at our conference in March.
lines.ko: 3월 저희 콘퍼런스에서 기조연설을 해 주신다면 영광이겠습니다.

lines.text: I'm genuinely flattered, and I wish the timing were different.
lines.ko: 진심으로 영광이고, 시기만 달랐다면 좋았을 텐데요.

lines.text: We're launching a product that month, and I couldn't give your audience the preparation they deserve.
lines.ko: 그달에 제품 출시가 있어서 청중에게 걸맞은 준비를 해 드릴 수 없을 것 같아요.

lines.text: If it helps, I'd be happy to recommend a colleague who speaks brilliantly on the topic.
lines.ko: 도움이 된다면 그 주제로 훌륭하게 발표하는 동료를 기꺼이 추천해 드릴게요.

phrases.en: I wish the timing were different.
The preparation they deserve.

response.situationKo: 동료가 주말 행사 진행을 부탁합니다. 관계를 지키며 거절해 보세요.
response.prompt: Would you be willing to host the charity dinner on Saturday?

answers.text: I'm honored you asked. Unfortunately, I have a family commitment that day.
I wish I could, but I'd hate to do it half-heartedly. Perhaps next year?
I can't host, but I'd be glad to help with the planning beforehand.
Oh, I'd love to, but Saturday's completely booked. Rain check?

title: Small talk with the CEO
settingKo: 엘리베이터에서 우연히 대표이사를 만나 짧게 대화합니다.

lines.text: You're on the data team, right? What's keeping you busy these days?
lines.ko: 데이터팀이죠? 요즘 뭐가 제일 바빠요?

lines.text: We're rebuilding the churn model. It already flags at-risk customers about two weeks earlier.
lines.ko: 이탈 모델을 다시 만들고 있어요. 이미 위험 고객을 2주쯤 더 빨리 잡아내요.

lines.text: Two weeks earlier? That could make a real difference for retention.
lines.ko: 2주나 빨리요? 유지율에 정말 큰 차이를 만들 수 있겠네요.

lines.text: That's the hope. I'd be glad to share the results with you once we've tested it properly.
lines.ko: 그게 목표예요. 제대로 검증되면 결과를 공유드릴게요.

phrases.en: What's keeping you busy these days?
Once we've tested it properly.

response.situationKo: 높은 사람이 갑자기 하는 일을 묻습니다. 30초 안에 인상적으로 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Remind me, what does your team work on?

answers.text: In short, we help customers find answers on their own, so support tickets dropped twenty percent this quarter.
We're responsible for onboarding. For example, we cut the time to first purchase in half.
We make the app faster. Last month's update made checkout two seconds quicker.
We work on pricing. Our latest test increased revenue per user without hurting sign-ups.

title: Not bad at all
settingKo: 영국인 동료의 돌려 말하는 화법을 미국인 동료가 설명해 줍니다.

lines.text: When Oliver said my proposal was quite interesting, I thought he liked it. Was I wrong?
lines.ko: 올리버가 내 제안이 꽤 흥미롭다고 해서 좋아하는 줄 알았어. 내가 틀렸어?

lines.text: Possibly. From a British colleague, quite interesting can mean they have serious doubts.
lines.ko: 아마도. 영국 동료가 꽤 흥미롭다고 하면 심각한 의구심이 있다는 뜻일 수 있어.

lines.text: And when he said with the greatest respect?
lines.ko: 그럼 '대단히 존경하지만'이라고 한 건?

lines.text: That usually means he thinks you're wrong. I'd ask him directly what concerns him most.
lines.ko: 그건 보통 네가 틀렸다는 뜻이야. 뭐가 제일 걱정되는지 직접 물어봐.

phrases.en: They have serious doubts.
With the greatest respect.

response.situationKo: 상대의 말이 칭찬인지 비판인지 애매합니다. 정중하게 진의를 확인해 보세요.
response.prompt: Well, it's certainly a brave idea.

answers.text: Just to be sure I understand, do you see any risks I might have missed?
answers.noteKo: Just to be sure로 부드럽게 확인해요.

answers.text: Could you say more about what concerns you? I'd value your honest view.
Brave in a good way, or brave as in risky?
I'm sensing some hesitation. What would make you more comfortable with it?

title: Disagreeing with a cofounder
settingKo: 회사의 방향을 두고 공동 창업자와 깊은 대화를 합니다.

lines.text: Every time we talk about raising money, it feels like we want two completely different companies.
lines.ko: 투자 얘기를 할 때마다 우리가 완전히 다른 두 회사를 원하는 것 같아.

lines.text: I think that's fair. You want to grow fast, and I want something sustainable we fully control.
lines.ko: 맞는 말이야. 너는 빨리 크고 싶고 나는 우리가 완전히 통제하는 지속 가능한 걸 원해.

lines.text: Neither of us is wrong, but we can't keep postponing this decision.
lines.ko: 둘 다 틀린 건 아니지만 이 결정을 계속 미룰 순 없어.

lines.text: Agreed. Let's bring in a neutral advisor and set a deadline for a decision we'll both respect.
lines.ko: 동의해. 중립적인 자문가를 부르고 둘 다 존중할 결정 기한을 정하자.

phrases.en: Neither of us is wrong.
We can't keep postponing this decision.
phrases.ko: 이 결정을 계속 미룰 순 없어.

response.situationKo: 오래 함께한 파트너와 의견이 갈립니다. 관계를 지키며 솔직하게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: I feel like you're not listening to me anymore.

answers.text: I'm sorry it feels that way. Help me understand what I've been missing.
What I'm hearing is that you feel overruled. Is that right?
That's not my intention at all. Let's slow down and go through it point by point.
Fair. I've been stressed and short with you. Let's grab dinner and really talk.

title: Offering condolences
settingKo: 어머니를 잃은 동료에게 조심스럽게 위로를 전합니다.

lines.text: I was so sorry to hear about your mother. Please don't feel you need to say anything.
lines.ko: 어머님 소식 듣고 정말 마음이 아팠어요. 아무 말 안 하셔도 괜찮아요.

lines.text: Thank you. It still doesn't feel real. Everyone's been very kind.
lines.ko: 고마워요. 아직 실감이 안 나요. 다들 정말 친절하게 대해 주셨어요.

lines.text: Take all the time you need, and I'll cover the client calls until you're ready to come back.
lines.ko: 필요한 만큼 시간을 가지세요. 돌아올 준비가 될 때까지 고객 통화는 제가 맡을게요.

lines.text: That means more than you know. I'll probably be back next Monday.
lines.ko: 생각보다 훨씬 큰 의미예요. 아마 다음 주 월요일에 돌아올 것 같아요.

gist.questionKo: 동료가 대신 해 주겠다고 한 것은?

phrases.en: Please don't feel you need to say anything.
That means more than you know.

response.situationKo: 친구가 반려동물을 떠나보냈습니다. 따뜻하게 위로해 보세요.
response.prompt: We had to say goodbye to our dog yesterday.

answers.text: I'm so sorry. She was lucky to have a family who loved her that much.
I'm truly sorry for your loss. I'm thinking of you all.
answers.noteKo: sorry for your loss는 정중한 조의 표현이에요.

answers.text: Oh no, that's heartbreaking. If you need anything, even just company, I'm here.
answers.noteKo: even just company는 곁에 있어 주는 것만이라도예요.

answers.text: I'm so sorry. He had such a gentle personality. I'll really miss him too.

title: A leader apologizes
settingKo: 회사 대표가 직원 전체 회의에서 잘못된 결정을 사과합니다.

lines.text: Last month I announced the new bonus structure without consulting any of you, and that was a mistake.
lines.ko: 지난달 여러분과 상의 없이 새 보너스 체계를 발표했고, 그건 실수였습니다.

lines.text: I've read every one of your comments, and many of them were uncomfortable but fair.
lines.ko: 여러분의 의견을 모두 읽었고, 많은 의견이 불편했지만 정당했습니다.

lines.text: So does that mean the old structure is coming back?
lines.ko: 그럼 예전 체계로 돌아간다는 건가요?

lines.text: For this year, yes. And we'll design next year's version together, with representatives from every team.
lines.ko: 올해는 그렇습니다. 그리고 내년 안은 모든 팀 대표와 함께 설계할 겁니다.

options: 올해는 예전 체계, 내년은 함께 설계

phrases.en: That was a mistake.
Uncomfortable but fair.

response.situationKo: 팀장으로서 팀에 잘못된 결정을 사과하고 바로잡겠다고 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why did you change the schedule without asking us?

answers.text: You're right. I should have asked first, and that's on me. Let's fix it together.
I apologize. Going forward, any change that affects your time will be discussed first.
Fair question, and there's no good excuse. I'll put the old schedule back today.
Honestly, I rushed it. My bad. What would work better for everyone?

title: Everything went wrong
settingKo: 폭풍으로 연결편이 모두 꼬여 항공사 직원과 일정을 다시 짭니다.

lines.text: My flight to Denver was canceled, so I'll miss the connection to Lima, and my tour starts the next morning.
lines.ko: 덴버행이 결항돼서 리마 연결편을 놓치고, 투어는 다음 날 아침에 시작해요.

lines.text: The storm has grounded most flights through Denver. Let me see if I can route you through Houston instead.
lines.ko: 폭풍으로 덴버 경유 항공편이 대부분 결항됐어요. 휴스턴 경유로 바꿀 수 있는지 볼게요.

lines.text: There's a seat leaving tonight that lands in Lima at six a.m., but it's in a middle seat.
lines.ko: 오늘 밤 출발해서 리마에 오전 6시 도착하는 자리가 있는데 가운데 좌석이에요.

lines.text: I'll take it. A middle seat is a small price to pay for not missing the whole tour.
lines.ko: 그걸로 할게요. 투어 전체를 놓치지 않는다면 가운데 자리쯤은 괜찮아요.

phrases.en: Route you through Houston instead.
A small price to pay.

response.situationKo: 항공사 직원이 내일 출발만 가능하다고 합니다. 가능한 대안을 모두 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: The earliest I can get you out is tomorrow afternoon.

answers.text: Is there any way to get me on a partner airline tonight, even with a stop?
Could you check flights from the nearby airport? I can take a train there.
What about standby on the earlier flight, in case someone doesn't show up?
Tomorrow afternoon kills my whole plan. Any creative options at all?
answers.noteKo: kills my plan은 계획이 망가진다는 뜻이에요.

title: Appealing a denied claim
settingKo: 의료비 보험 청구가 거절되어 이의를 제기합니다.

lines.text: My claim for the MRI was denied as not medically necessary, but my doctor ordered it after two months of pain.
lines.ko: MRI 청구가 의학적으로 불필요하다고 거절됐는데 두 달간 통증 후 의사가 지시한 거예요.

lines.text: I understand. To appeal, we'll need a letter from your doctor explaining why the scan was required.
lines.ko: 이해합니다. 이의 신청을 하려면 왜 검사가 필요했는지 설명하는 의사 소견서가 필요해요.

lines.text: She's already written one. Is there a deadline I should be aware of?
lines.ko: 이미 써 주셨어요. 알아야 할 기한이 있나요?

lines.text: You have sixty days from the denial date, and we usually respond within thirty.
lines.ko: 거절일로부터 60일 이내이고, 보통 30일 안에 답변드려요.

phrases.en: It was denied as not medically necessary.
Is there a deadline I should be aware of?

response.situationKo: 상담원이 규정만 반복합니다. 논리적으로 재검토를 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: I'm afraid the decision is final according to our guidelines.

answers.text: I'd like to request a formal review. Could you tell me specifically which guideline was applied?
Could you put the reason for the denial in writing, so my doctor can respond to it?
I understand that's your guidance, but I'd like this escalated to a medical reviewer.
Final? There must be an appeals process. Walk me through it, please.
answers.noteKo: Walk me through it은 '차근차근 알려 주세요'예요.

title: A retirement toast
settingKo: 30년 근무한 선배의 은퇴식에서 축사를 합니다.

lines.text: When I joined this company twelve years ago, Maria was the first person who took me seriously.
lines.ko: 12년 전 이 회사에 들어왔을 때 저를 진지하게 대해 준 첫 사람이 마리아였어요.

lines.text: She taught me that you can be demanding and kind at the same time, and that it's rarer than it should be.
lines.ko: 까다로우면서도 동시에 친절할 수 있다는 걸, 그리고 그게 생각보다 드물다는 걸 가르쳐 줬죠.

lines.text: Oh, stop, you'll make me cry before dessert.
lines.ko: 아이고 그만해, 디저트 나오기도 전에 울겠어.

lines.text: Thirty years, countless mentees, and not a single deadline missed. To Maria, and to whatever comes next!
lines.ko: 30년, 셀 수 없는 후배들, 놓친 마감은 단 한 번도 없었죠. 마리아와 그녀의 다음 여정을 위하여!

phrases.en: She was the first person who took me seriously.
phrases.ko: 저를 진지하게 대해 준 첫 사람이었어요.

phrases.en: To Maria, and to whatever comes next!

response.situationKo: 떠나는 동료에게 짧은 감사의 건배사를 해 보세요.
response.prompt: Would you like to say a few words before we raise our glasses?

answers.text: I'd just like to say thank you for always making time for us. Here's to your next chapter!
You taught me more than any training ever could. We'll miss you enormously. Cheers!
On behalf of the whole team, thank you for your patience, your humor, and your coffee. To Sam!
Who's going to fix the printer now? Seriously, we'll miss you. Cheers!

title: Announcing layoffs
settingKo: 임원이 팀장들에게 구조 조정 계획을 미리 알립니다.

lines.text: Before Friday's announcement, I wanted you to hear it from me. We're reducing headcount by about eight percent.
lines.ko: 금요일 발표 전에 저한테 직접 듣기를 원했어요. 인원을 약 8퍼센트 줄입니다.

lines.text: How were the roles chosen? My team will want to know it wasn't arbitrary.
lines.ko: 어떤 기준으로 정했나요? 팀원들은 자의적이지 않았다는 걸 알고 싶어 할 거예요.

lines.text: It's based on which projects we're stopping, not individual performance, and everyone affected gets four months' pay.
lines.ko: 개인 성과가 아니라 중단하는 프로젝트 기준이고, 대상자 모두 4개월 치 급여를 받아요.

lines.text: That's more than I expected. I'd like to tell my people myself, in person, on Friday morning.
lines.ko: 예상보다 많네요. 금요일 아침에 제가 직접 팀원들에게 말하고 싶어요.

phrases.en: I wanted you to hear it from me.
It wasn't arbitrary.

response.situationKo: 불안해하는 팀원이 회사 사정을 묻습니다. 정직하지만 차분하게 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Are there going to be more cuts? Should I be worried?

answers.text: I understand the worry. What I can tell you is that no further cuts are planned right now.
answers.noteKo: What I can tell you is로 아는 것만 말해요.

answers.text: Honestly, I don't know everything, but I promise I'll be transparent with you as soon as I hear anything.
answers.noteKo: 모른다는 걸 인정하는 것도 신뢰를 줘요.

answers.text: It's normal to feel that way. Let's talk about what's in your control, like the projects we're keeping.
I'd tell you if I knew. Right now, your role looks solid. Let's grab coffee and talk it through.

title: Managing up
settingKo: 현실성 없는 목표를 정한 상사에게 조심스럽게 의견을 냅니다.

lines.text: I fully support the goal of doubling sign-ups, but I'm not sure we can get there by June with the current team.
lines.ko: 가입자 두 배 목표는 전적으로 지지하지만 지금 인원으로 6월까지 가능할지 모르겠어요.

lines.text: What would it take, realistically?
lines.ko: 현실적으로 뭐가 필요해요?

lines.text: Either two more engineers, or we narrow the scope and target the three markets with the most potential.
lines.ko: 엔지니어 두 명을 더 쓰거나, 범위를 좁혀서 잠재력이 가장 큰 세 시장에 집중하는 거요.

lines.text: Hiring will take months. Put together a plan for the narrower option and let's review it Thursday.
lines.ko: 채용은 몇 달 걸려요. 범위 축소안으로 계획을 짜서 목요일에 검토해요.

phrases.en: What would it take, realistically?
We narrow the scope.

response.situationKo: 상사가 무리한 마감을 정했어요. 반대하지 않고 대안을 제시해 보세요.
response.prompt: I need the full redesign live by next Friday.
keywords: i want to make that happen

answers.text: I want to make that happen. To do that, we'd need to pause the mobile work for two weeks.
Alternatively, we could launch the homepage by Friday and the rest the week after.
There's a trade-off between speed and quality here. Which matters most for this launch?
Doable if we cut corners somewhere. Which corners are you OK with?

title: On a panel about climate
settingKo: 기후 변화 패널 토론에서 사회자의 질문에 답합니다.

lines.text: Critics say individual actions like recycling are a distraction from what governments and corporations should be doing. Do you agree?
lines.ko: 재활용 같은 개인의 행동은 정부와 기업이 해야 할 일에서 시선을 돌리게 한다는 비판이 있어요. 동의하세요?

lines.text: Partly. Individual choices alone won't solve it, but they shape the norms that make policy politically possible.
lines.ko: 부분적으로요. 개인의 선택만으로는 해결 못 하지만 정책을 정치적으로 가능하게 하는 규범을 만들어요.

lines.text: So you see them as complementary rather than competing?
lines.ko: 그럼 경쟁이 아니라 상호 보완으로 보시는 거군요?

lines.text: Exactly. The real danger is when companies use individual responsibility as an excuse to avoid regulation.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 진짜 위험은 기업이 개인의 책임을 규제를 피하는 핑계로 쓸 때예요.

phrases.en: Complementary rather than competing.
An excuse to avoid regulation.

response.situationKo: 사회 문제에 대해 질문을 받습니다. 균형 잡히고 논리적으로 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Should cities ban cars from their centers entirely?

answers.text: In principle, yes, but only once public transport is reliable enough to replace them.
I'd argue for a gradual approach. Sudden bans tend to hurt small businesses most.
The evidence from cities like Oslo is encouraging; however, every city's geography is different.
Honestly, it depends. A ban works in a compact old town, not in a sprawling city.

title: Applying for a grant
settingKo: 연구비 지원서를 동료와 함께 다듬습니다.

lines.text: The science is strong, but the reviewers will want to know why this matters to people outside our field.
lines.ko: 과학적으론 탄탄한데, 심사위원들은 이게 우리 분야 밖의 사람들에게 왜 중요한지 알고 싶어 할 거예요.

lines.text: Good point. We could open with the impact on early diagnosis rather than the method itself.
lines.ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 방법론보다 조기 진단에 미치는 영향으로 시작하면 되겠네요.

lines.text: And cut the background section in half. Right now the actual proposal doesn't start until page four.
lines.ko: 그리고 배경 부분을 절반으로 줄여요. 지금은 실제 제안이 4쪽에야 시작해요.

lines.text: Fair. I'll have a revised draft to you by Wednesday so we have time for one more round.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 한 번 더 검토할 시간이 있게 수요일까지 수정안을 드릴게요.

phrases.en: Why this matters to people outside our field.
So we have time for one more round.

response.prompt: Could you give me honest feedback on my report before I send it?
